ui_bugs.issue: The pre-submit amber qualification warning 'create-qualif-warning' NEVER appears in the create-task dialog when an unqualified employee is selected. The div is bound to `createQualifWarning = tAssignee!=='team' && tTitle && (caps[tAssignee]??[]).length > 0 && !isQualified(...)`, but the `caps` state (line 67: `const [caps, setCaps] = useState<Record<string,string[]>>({})`) is declared and NEVER populated — there is no axios call to fetch employee capacities from `/api/profiles/{employee_id}`. Consequently `(caps[tAssignee] ?? []).length > 0` is always false, and the amber banner never renders before submit. The POST-submit sonner toast + card badge task-qualif-warning-{id} DO work correctly (both driven by the backend's qualification_warning flag), so the feature is only half-implemented on the frontend.

action_items: In /app/frontend/src/components/modules/TasksModule.tsx, populate the `caps` state by fetching employee capacities (e.g., an axios useEffect calling GET /api/profiles/{id} for each active employee, or GET /api/profiles bulk). Without this, the specified 'avertissement ambre dans le dialogue de création' feature never triggers pre-submit — only post-submit toast + card badge work. Consider triggering the fetch lazily when tAssignee changes and cache in caps state to avoid N calls.

rca_of_the_issue: The `create-qualif-warning` bug is a straightforward missing-fetch: `TasksModule.tsx` line 67 declares `const [caps, setCaps] = useState<Record<string,string[]>>({})` but no code path ever calls setCaps. Grep for 'caps|setCaps|capacities|profiles' in that file returns only the declaration, the usage inside `createQualifWarning`, and the type of the local helper `isQualified` — no axios.get for /api/profiles. Fix by adding a useEffect (deps: [tAssignee]) that fetches the selected employee's profile and merges capacities into `caps`, OR fetch all profiles once on mount. Alternatively, compute qualification locally by mirroring backend's title vs. employee.position/capacities from HRContext (though HRContext currently only exposes basic Employee data — capacities live on profile documents, not on employees list).
